events.title: U.S. Consumer Sentiment Deteriorates Far Less Than Previously Estimated In October
events.description: The University of Michigan released a report on Friday showing consumer sentiment in the U.S. deteriorated by far less than previously estimated in the month of October. The report said the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index for October was upwardly revised to 48.0 from a preliminary reading of 46.3.

events.title: Bay Street Look Headed For Weak Start
events.description:
Canadian stocks are likely to open on a weak note on Friday amid concerns about inflation and prospects of interest rate hikes by the Canadian and U.S. central banks. Oil prices are up sharply, while precious metals are notably lower.

Canadian retail sales data, and quarterly earnings updates, as well as U.S. PMI reports are set to make a notable impact on price movements.

events.title: Eurozone Private Sector Growth At 4-Month Low
events.description: The euro area private sector softened to a four-month low in October as activity in France shifted back into contraction amid tightening financial conditions and rising political pressures, flash purchasing managers' survey data from S&P Global revealed Friday. The composite output index fell to 51.9 in October from 53.1 in the previous month, falling below the economist forecast of 52.7.

events.title: FTSE 100 Falls 0.5% On Weak Retail Sales, Consumer Confidence Data
events.description: The FTSE 100 declined 52.73 points to 10,672.32 Friday as weak retail sales, declining consumer confidence, and Middle East tensions offset private sector expansion. Retail sales fell 0.4% in September versus forecasts of 0.1%, while consumer sentiment hit its sharpest pandemic-era drop.

events.title: French Benchmark Weakens On Earnings, Economic Contraction
events.description: France's CAC 40 equity benchmark declined 0.67% Friday as investors reacted to disappointing corporate earnings and flash data revealing contraction in the nation's services sector during October. Middle East tensions and elevated oil prices weighed on sentiment.

events.title: Indian Shares Extend Losses For Fourth Day
events.description: Indian shares gave up early gains to end lower on Friday, extending losses for a fourth consecutive session due to concerns over rising oil prices and expectations of higher-for-longer interest rates.

events.title: DAX Down Nearly 1% As Middle East Tensions, AI Concerns Weigh On Stocks
events.description: German stocks declined Friday as Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and uncertainty surrounding AI investment returns weighed on sentiment. The DAX fell 237.50 points to 25,134.25. Manufacturing PMI rose to 54.2, beating expectations, while services PMI fell to 51.7.

events.title: Gold Headed For Steep Weekly Loss On Oil-driven Inflation Concerns
events.description: Gold held steady on Friday but headed for its steepest weekly loss in over four months as a result of rising oil prices and higher-for-longer interest rate expectations.

events.title: NZ Dollar Rises Amid RBNZ Rate Hike Prospects
events.description: The New Zealand dollar strengthened against other major currencies in the Asian session on Friday, amid growing expectations of a Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) rate hike in the upcoming monetary policy meetings.

events.title: Oil Headed For Third Weekly Gain
events.description: Oil prices surged to a five-month high on Friday amid concerns over further disruption to energy supplies following Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure and Red Sea ports.

events.title: European Shares Edge Lower In Cautious Trade
events.description: European stocks traded lower on Friday and headed for a weekly loss amid renewed concerns about France's finances, continued Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, and doubts over whether hyperscalers' massive AI investments will yield adequate returns.

events.title: Asian Shares Mixed In Choppy Trade
events.description: Asian stocks ended mixed on Friday due to concerns over technology valuations and escalating Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.

events.title: UK Retail Sales Fall More Than Forecast
events.description: UK retail sales declined more than expected in September as warm weather weighed on clothing and supermarket sales, data released by the Office for National Statistics showed on Friday. Retail sales decreased 0.4 percent in September, reversing a rise of 0.7 percent in August and exceeded economists' forecast of a 0.1 percent fall.
